Christopher Baum

Approval Voting candidate for United States Senator, Colorado · Challenger

Retired U.S. Navy commander; former small-business owner and computer network administrator

Christopher Baum is the Approval Voting Party nominee for U.S. Senate in Colorado in the November 3, 2026 general election. He is a retired Navy commander based in Denver who served from 1967 to 1987. He ran for the Colorado House, District 34, in 2022 and for Colorado's 8th Congressional District in 2024.

Where Baum stands

Health care / Medicaid
Says taxpayer-funded health care should be abolished in all forms and Medicaid and Medicare defunded; argues medical care is an individual responsibility under the 10th Amendment.
Immigration enforcement
Opposes sanctuary cities; says tolerating illegal immigration means 'we might as well not have laws.'
Legal immigration
Says anyone should be allowed to immigrate if they pass screening to ensure they will not subvert U.S. principles.
Term limits
Proposes limiting representatives and senators to two terms, eliminating their pensions, and barring them from working for government contractors for five years after leaving office.
Climate / energy
Names nuclear power as the most reliable energy source to meet growing electricity demand.
Federal spending and debt
Supports cutting spending to reduce the national debt, balancing budgets every year, prohibiting government debt except in wartime, and eliminating government grants.
Foreign policy
Says the U.S. should selectively help countries trying to build democracy and fight tyranny; supports helping Israel and calls the Chinese Communist Party a serious threat.
Abortion
Says human life deserves legal protection from conception and elective abortion should never be allowed; opposes taxpayer funding for abortion providers. Says abortion drugs should be allowed when medically indicated.
Education
Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education; says no government should fund education and that it is a matter for parents.
Guns
Says no restrictions on gun ownership are needed, citing citizens' right to protect themselves from criminals and from government.

Background

  • Approval Voting Party nominee, U.S. Senate, Colorado (2026)
  • Candidate, U.S. House, Colorado District 8 (2024; about 1.7% of the vote)
  • Candidate, Colorado House of Representatives, District 34 (2022)
  • U.S. Navy, 1967–1987; retired as commander
  • Former interior decorating shop owner; former network administrator for the New Mexico Bar Association
  • President, Kiwanis Club of Albuquerque (per candidate, 1987–2009)
  • ScB, Brown University (1967); Master of Governmental Administration, University of Pennsylvania (1979)
  • Has held no elected office
